claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating has a fine-grained microstructure.
Annealing the coating at approximately 500°C before wear will form a thin, continuous, adherent oxide scale.
Pre-wear annealing at approximately 500°C will cause moderate grain coarsening in FeNiCrCoCu.
Grain coarsening is deleterious to the coating's high-temperature wear resistance.
Thermally induced grain growth typically lowers hardness.
The annealing-induced oxide layer will act as a lubricious barrier.
The oxide barrier will reduce friction and material removal by mitigating direct contact wear.
Protection supplied by the oxide scale will outweigh the adverse effect of grain coarsening if the scale is adequately formed.
Pre-annealed FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a lower coefficient of friction than non-annealed coatings during high-temperature wear.
Pre-annealed FeNiCrCoCu coatings will exhibit less wear loss than non-annealed coatings during high-temperature wear.
The proposed mechanism applies from 300°C to 600°C under a mechanical load of approximately 26 N.
Outside the specified temperature range, temperature-dependent oxide formation may change the balance between oxidation protection and grain coarsening.
The relative effects of oxide formation and grain coarsening may depend on annealing duration and environmental conditions.
